thread.title: Daimler ( OTCPK:DDAIF ) just released record results for FY2

author: Stefan Redlich
title: Daimler ( OTCPK:DDAIF ) just released record results for FY2
text:
Daimler ( OTCPK:DDAIF ) just released record results for FY2017 but its stock price reacted unimpressed and went south on concerns about margin pressure and that it will be tough for Daimler to repeat that performance going forward. 
Daimler generated lots of cash in 2017 but its stock enjoyed a dismal year. The company hiked its dividend by an unprecedented 12% and is yielding 5% again. 
Internally, a lot of things are going on. Not only is Daimler reported to be working on establishing a new corporate structure but it is also making substantial investments into future technologies and it is rumored that Chinese investor Geely is about to make a large investment. 
In this article we will review Daimler's latest financial results, its strategy, its dividend, the intended restructuring and of course what a Geely investment could bring to the stock.

Source: Future Truck 2025: The first self-driving truck by Mercedes-Benz 
What is going on at Daimler? Daimler just posted record results for 2017 with group EBIT increasing by 14% to €14.7B and revenue rising by 7% to €164.3B. Net profit surged even more with a gain of 24% and easily topped the €10B barrier coming in at €10.9B.
The Mercedes Brand continues to grow at a high single-digit clip as the company sold 2.4 million cars (+8%) with growth in China exploding by 28% and exceeding the 500,000 unit sales barrier for the first time. Trucks, vans and buses grew even stronger between 9% to 13% and were only topped by a 14% growth in Daimler Financial Services. 
A very strong product portfolio in all of Daimler's business segments helped achieve continued business growth. A crucial development for Daimler's future as it is approaching its entry point for self-driving car services is the Daimler Mobility Services segment. Its two-car sharing services now count 17.8M customers in more than 100 cities. Daimler does not release any detailed financial figures for this segment but the overall goals are to extend the Daimler ecosystem, grow its customer base, understand the needs of its customers and thereby help prepare for the future. This is Daimler's pioneering initiative " in the future area of shared and services " as mentioned by member of the Board of Management Bodo Uebber. 
Daimler spends €8.7B on R&D epitomizing its core strategy to innovate technologies and modern production facilities. That's a record amount of R&D spending which will increase further in 2018.
Despite a record year net liquidity declined by €3.1B to €16.6B which is entirely explained by an extraordinary contribution of €3B to the German pension plan assets. Disregarding that impact Daimler's free cash flow would have been €5.0B. Daimler paid an annual dividend of €3.25 in 2017 which results in a FCF dividend payout ratio of 70%. That's a very reasonable payout ratio considering Daimler's massive R&D spending in 2017 and provides room for future dividend increases. 
That R&D spending also is a prime reason why Daimler's 2018 business outlook came short of expectations. It is guiding for a slight increase in unit sales and revenue at a similar EBIT as in 2017. 
As a result and due to a general market sale the stock declined to around €71 now trading at a forward dividend yield of 5.1%. Not having raised the dividend for FY 2016 I was expecting the market to appreciate such a strong dividend raise for FY 2017. However, as was not the case this has now given Daimler an even more attractive valuation. It is the highest-yielding stock in the DAX (currently) and is only trading at round 8 times forward earnings.

In terms of strategy Daimler is executing its Leadership 2020 strategy termed "The future of corporate culture."

Source: Daimler Corporate Presentation / Q2 2017 / page 37 
One of the most important targets is to become the No.1 premium car manufacturer. Daimler belongs at the top and therefore is targeting at least 10% return on sales on a sustainable basis. For FY2017 its return on sales for Mercedes-Benz cars already was at 9.7% and thus 0.6pp higher than 2016. Daimler is on the right track to achieve its target. 
The company is aggressively investing into future technologies like autonomous driving, digitizing ecosystems, and it is providing service platforms along tomorrow's mobility value chain.

Source: Daimler Corporate Presentation / Q2 2017 / page 75 
Daimler's strategy is sound and clear and its financial fire power, experience and scale should allow it to deliver. This is a highly sophisticated strategy which shows that Daimler is making the necessary steps to position itself perfectly along the value chain.

Source: Daimler Corporate Presentation / Q2 2017 / page 86 
What's more, although details are still scarce, it has been confirmed by Daimler that it's planning to reorganize itself into a holding . The goal of this is to make Daimler more flexible to respond to developments in the automotive sector and streamline the company for its 2020 strategy. A proposed setup envisions three pillars: Mercedes-Benz Cars and Vans, Trucks and Buses and Financial Services. The goal is not to split up the company but to allow for partial IPOs, if any at all. This should result in cost synergies and could also lead to higher valuations of the individual units instead of valuing them all in one. What's remarkable is that although Daimler has not fully committed itself to such a separation of business segments it has already granted a collective job guarantee until 2029. This gives the company the security that its powerful works council is not torpedoing any plans and instead helps gain more buy-in. Final decisions are expected not to happen before its annual shareholders meeting in 2019.
Here comes Geely On February 2 news broke that Chinese investor Li Shufu is about to make a sizable investment into Daimler via the parent company of Volvo Cars, Geely ( GELYF ). The stock reacted unimpressed to that news but it could be big news for the company and its stockholders. The economic reasoning behind Geely striking a deal at or above 5% (this is the threshold which requires a public press release) is to form a strategic alliance against America's leading tech companies Google ( GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Apple ( AAPL ). Although Daimler already is making massive investments into technology and software these companies have even more financial fire power to enter the vast future market of connected and self-driving cars. Having another strong partner would certainly be helpful for Daimler. Currently, its largest investor is Kuwait's sovereign wealth fund with a 6.8% stake. 
Investor Takeaway Overall, Daimler's stock is a bit of a mystery . On the one hand you have a company with one record year after another, with a superb dividend, an ultra-low valuation and great products. On the other hand, concerns about a potential future disruption of the automobile industry, Daimler's potential manipulation of emission values and fears that tiny and inefficient competitors such as Tesla ( TSLA ) could snap substantial market share. 
Personally, I continue to believe that investors are overconfident in what Tesla can achieve and put too much value on potential litigation payments associated with collusion accusations. Even if the latter turns out to be true, Daimler's cash position should allow it to rather safely maneuver through this phase while at the same time cementing its status as the world's leading premium car manufacturer. Daimler has the financial resources, the human resources and the production capabilities to react to a changing market. And having another strong investor at its side with Geely as it is rumored should further ease concerns. 
Investors believing in this thesis continue to find an attractive entry opportunity in the stock right now and can lock in a 5.1% yield . Should the strength of the euro continue Daimler's international profits may grow less but U.S. investors can benefit from foreign exchange profits. I also like the preferred shares of BMW ( OTCPK:BMWYY ), trading at a similarly low valuation and comparable dividend yield. Also, BMW is yet to report financial year 2017 results and its next dividend which is scheduled for March 21. Based on an expected 10% dividend raise the forward dividend yield would be 5% as well. 
You should not expect any quick stock price appreciation for both Daimler and BMW but the dividend and future prospects should compensate for that. Trading at such a low valuation with a juicy yield is a very attractive setup for long-term investors.
